name: Gmail
short_description: Search threads, read messages, and draft replies in Gmail directly from your agent.
store_description: Google's official hosted Gmail MCP server (Workspace Developer Preview). IMPORTANT: This server requires manual setup before it can be used. (1) Join the Google Workspace Developer Preview Program at https://developers.google.com/workspace/preview. (2) In your Google Cloud project, enable BOTH APIs: 'gmail.googleapis.com' (the REST API) and 'gmailmcp.googleapis.com' (the MCP service). (3) Create an OAuth 2.0 Client ID (Web application) at https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials with redirect URI 'http://127.0.0.1:3088/api/mcp/oauth/callback'. (4) In Google Auth Platform > Clients, open the OAuth client and check 'Use this client for an AI-powered agent'. This flag is MANDATORY from November 11, 2026 — Google will reject any OAuth client without it. (5) Set PELDRUN_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and PELDRUN_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET environment variables. (6) Add your Google account as a test user on the OAuth consent screen. Once configured, the server exposes read-only Gmail tools by default: gmail_search_threads, gmail_get_thread, gmail_list_labels, gmail_get_profile. Adding 'gmail.modify' to the scopes list enables drafting and label modification.
description: Official Gmail MCP server — search, read, and draft emails.
usage_hint: Gmail MCP exposes read-only tools by default. WORKFLOW: (1) When the user references an email by subject/sender/date but you do not have an ID, call gmail_search_threads with a Gmail query (same syntax as the Gmail search box, e.g. 'from:alice@example.com newer_than:7d subject:invoice'). (2) Call gmail_get_thread with the returned threadId to fetch the full conversation. (3) Use gmail_list_labels when the user asks about folders. (4) Use gmail_get_profile when the user asks 'which account am I signed in as'. To enable drafting and sending, add 'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify' to the scopes list and re-authorize — Google will present a new consent screen because prompt=consent is enforced by PELDRUN for Google providers.
